Before
 Hon'Ble Shri Justice Gajendra Singh
 Misc. Appeal No. 1537 of 2022
 Vijay Chouhan And Others
 Versus
 Vijay Sankhla And Others
 Appearance:

Shri Gaurav Sharma, learned counsel for the appellants.
 Shri Mayank Upadhyay, learned counsel for the respondent [R-2  Reserved on 09.08.2024  Pronounced on 13.09.2024  --------------------------------------------------------
 ORDER

This miscellaneous appeal under section 173(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act is preferred being aggrieved by the award dated 03.08.2021 passed in MACC No.362/2018 by 10th Additional MACT,
Ujjain for enhancement of Rs.10 lakhs as compensation .

2. Facts in brief are that a claim under section 166(1) of the Motor Vehicles Act , 1988 was preferred by the claimants for compensation of Rs.60,50,000/- with 12% interest per annum regarding death of their son Rahul, aged 22 years working as Production Manager in D.P Plastic, Ratlam and was earning Rs.30,000/- per month who sustained injuries in motor vehicle accident on 23.12.2017 at 09.45 a.m by negligent driving of alto car no.MP-11-CC-1873 owned and driven by respondent no.1 and insured with respondent no.2.
3.

The claim was contested by respondent no.2 insurance company and NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2024:MPHC-IND:26528 2 MA-1537-2022

appreciating the evidence tribunal awarded a total compensation of Rs.13,91,200/- estimating his income as Rs.7,125/- and deducting 1/2 for personal expenses as the deceased was bachelor and applying the multiplier of 18 as the age of the deceased was between 21 to 25 years and adding 40% income as future prospects and thus calculated the total loss of dependency at Rs.10,77,300/-.
The tribunal has also added Rs.2,43,900/- towards medical expenses, Rs.15,000/- towards funeral expenses, Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium and Rs.15,000/- towards loss of estate.

4. Challenging the compensation this appeal has been preferred on the ground that the appointment letter Ex.P/30 and salary certificate Ex.P/119 have not been taken into consideration by the tribunal.

It has also not been taken into consideration that the deceased Rahul was well educated.
5. Counsel for the respondent has opposed the prayer.

6. Perused the record.
7.
Ex . P/105C

to P/118C are the certificates regarding the educational qualification of the deceased Rahul and those documents disclose that the date of birth of Rahul was 21.12.1994 and he passed the High School Certificate Examination in the year 2010, the Higher Secondary School Certificate Examination in the year 2012 in first division and also completed his BE (Electronics &
Communication) from Rajiv Gandhi Proudyogiki Vishwavidyalaya, Bhopal in the 2016 and also participated in workshop relating to his professional career.
8. Ex.P/119 is submitted to demonstate that he was offered from D.P Plastic, Ratlam to join on 01.12.2017 for a salary of Rs.23,500/- per month but he succumbed to injuries.
The above description of the deceased reveals that the deceased has attained certainty.

In such type of cases the Apex Court has assessed Rs.20,000/- per NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26528 3 MA-1537-2022 month as income in the case of Basanti Devi and another vs. Divisional Manager,
New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - LL 2021 SC 728.
9.

New India Assurance Co. Ltd. - LL 2021 SC 728
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
In this case also the income of the deceased is assessed as Rs.20,000/- per month and added 40%
income towards loss of future prospects.
Accordingly, the loss of dependency in the present case comes to Rs.30,24,000/- (i.e. Rs.20000 - 1/2 PE=10000+40% FP=14000x12=1,68,000 x 18 (M)).
The tribunal has awarded only Rs.40,000/- towards loss of consortium whereas both parents have to be awarded consortium.
Accordingly, a sum of Rs.40,000/- is further added under the head of consortium.

Thus, the compensation is recalculated as under:
 Loss of dependency Rs.30,24,000/-
 Medical expenses Rs.2,43,900/-
 Loss of consortium Rs.80,000/-

Funeral expenses Rs.15,000/-
 Loss of estate Rs.15,000/-

. Accordingly, the appellants are entitled to an additional sum of Rs.19,86,700/-
over and above the amount which has been awarded by the Tribunal.
In the result, the appeal is allowed.
The enhanced amount shall bear interest at the same rate as awarded by the Tribunal.
The other findings recorded by the Tribunal shall remain intact.
11. The appellants have valued the appeal only to the extent of Rs.10 lakhs and paid the Court fee accordingly.

Therefore, for the remaining amount, the Court fee shall be paid by the appellants Vijay Chouhan vs Vijay Sankhla on 9 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/40835745/
2 within a period of one month and thereafter the amount shall be released by the Insurance Company on receiving the certificate.

In case the certificate has not been filed before the Insurance Company up to a period of three months, the claimant NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2024:MPHC-IND:26528 4 MA-1537-2022 shall not be entitled to receive the interest on the enhanced amount of compensation.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE hk/
